summary: Add lightweight server-side t() translation helper for Server Components

ai.s: Adds a server-side t() translation helper so Server Components can resolve i18n keys directly, removing the temporary NoAccessTranslated client wrapper.
ai.pr: Server Components cannot call useTranslation(), so a stop-gap client wrapper was added just to translate static strings, adding hydration and hiding the real i18n key from callsites.
ai.wy: Frontend tech debt: every future Server Component needing a translated string would otherwise need a client wrapper or ship raw English.
ai.oc: A memoised getServerTranslation(locale) helper is planned, with NoAccessTranslated removed and the 8 affected pages using the server t(), with no visual change.

summary: Bypass Payment Step When Basket Total Is £0 in Booking/Category Upgrade Flow

ai.s: Attendees whose basket total drops to £0 in the booking or category upgrade flow can complete the booking without being asked for payment or billing details.
ai.pr: When a 100% discount reduced the basket to £0 in booking or category upgrade, attendees still saw a "Pay £0.00" button and the payment form.
ai.wy: Asking for payment details on a free transaction is confusing friction for attendees and inconsistent with free registrations elsewhere.
ai.oc: A "Complete Booking" button replaces "Pay £0.00", the payment form is bypassed and a £0 invoice is sent only if the event's zero-price invoice setting is on.

summary: Kiosk Badge Export

ai.s: Organisers can export Kiosk badge printing data for attendees and exhibitor team members to Excel, showing unique and total prints per person.
ai.pr: Organisers had no export of Kiosk badge printing activity, so they could not analyse stationery usage or onsite printing per person.
ai.wy: Organisers need print data to track stationery usage and onsite activity during and after the live event.
ai.oc: A new "Kiosk" option under Data > Import/Export > Export produces a date-filtered .xlsx with per-person print counts and a timestamp per print.

summary: LexChat: self-host lexchat.js instead of loading from external siteURL

ai.s: Serves the LexChat chatbot script from the platform's own origin instead of loading it at runtime from the legacy external siteURL bundle.
ai.pr: The chatbot script loaded from an external new_assets host, so it could silently fail if that host was slow or blocked, had no version pinning and complicated a strict CSP.
ai.wy: Frontend tech debt and reliability: remove an unpinned runtime dependency on an external host and simplify CSP.
ai.oc: lexchat.js is to be vendored and served under the /newfront base path, with the Script src no longer interpolating siteURL and the chatbot initialising unchanged.

summary: [Tech Debt][Android] GDPR/excluded (scanned) bypass applied inconsistently in Exhibitor profile meeting gate

ai.s: Makes the Android exhibitor profile apply the same GDPR scanned-contact bypass as the personal profile, so the Meet button no longer disappears for scanned team members.
ai.pr: With GDPR checks on, a scanned single team member with gdpr = 0 showed Meet on their personal profile but "meetings not available" on the exhibitor profile, because the excluded check was missing.
ai.wy: The two profiles contradicted each other, blocking legitimate meeting requests and confusing users.
ai.oc: The exhibitor profile meeting gate is to include the scanned/excluded status, so Meet availability matches the personal profile.

summary: [TechDept] Research and fix admin permission-zone security issues (BAC, CSRF, XSS)

ai.s: Re-verifies the 2018 security notes on admin permission zones against today's code and plans or makes fixes for confirmed access-control, CSRF and XSS issues.
ai.pr: Admin pages tagged in 2018 with security problems were never tracked in Jira, and a 2026 spot-check found the CSRF gaps largely still real.
ai.wy: Security risk reduction: confirmed access-control and CSRF weaknesses in the admin panel need to be fixed or tracked.
ai.oc: Each tagged zone is to be marked still-real or already-fixed, with similar issues grouped and fixes made or split into assigned sub-tasks.

summary: Translation: please apply the missing system translations.

ai.s: Applies missing and corrected system translations, chiefly German, across exhibitor profile, registration photo, product list and notification screens.
ai.pr: Several screens showed wrong or missing German system translations, including team-member limit messages with broken number placeholders and badly worded registration photo labels.
ai.wy: Correct localisation for German-speaking events such as Hamburg Messe and Frankfurter Buchmesse tenants.
ai.oc: The listed EN/DE strings were decomposed into child tickets and corrected; the story is in testing.

summary: Resolve circular dependencies in portal-ui module graph (60 cycles)

ai.s: Breaks the 60 circular dependencies in the portal-ui module graph and adds a CI check so new cycles cannot creep back in.
ai.pr: madge reported 60 circular dependencies in portal-ui, 43 of them through the store barrel, risking undefined imports, fragile initialisation order and a larger bundle.
ai.wy: Frontend tech debt: cycles defeat tree-shaking, slow hot reload and cause load-order bugs.
ai.oc: Store barrel imports are to be replaced by direct slice imports, type-only cycles converted to import type, and a madge --circular CI check with a shrinking allowlist added.

summary: [iOS] Refactor project into multi-module SPM packages

ai.s: Refactors the iOS app project into multi-module Swift Package Manager packages (ticket has no further detail).
ai.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
ai.wy: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
ai.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to split the iOS codebase into separate SPM modules.

summary: API V3 Logs Admin Panel - UI Enhancements: Top Menu Button & Advanced Search

ai.s: Adds a top-menu shortcut to the API V3 Logs page and a stackable Advanced Search that filters logs by params, request body or response content.
ai.pr: After EP-50318 the V3 Logs page was only reachable by manual navigation and its filters could not search inside request or response payloads.
ai.wy: Two improvements proposed on EP-50318 were not yet actioned; support staff need to find specific API calls quickly.
ai.oc: A top navigation button is planned for all backend users, plus AND-combined conditions with Contains / Does not contain / == / != operators over serialised JSON.

summary: [TechDept] [EP] IDOR in ProfileController::signDocumentAction — buyer can sign/download any document via web endpoint

ai.s: Closes an IDOR in the hosted buyer Sign button endpoint so a buyer can no longer sign or download documents belonging to other categories or events.
ai.pr: POST /profile/signDocument accepted any document id without checking the buyer's category or event, letting a buyer render foreign documents to PDF.
ai.wy: Security: a major broken object-level authorisation flaw (CWE-639) on the endpoint the production web UI uses.
ai.oc: The endpoint is to get an allow-list check, an event-scope check and an isBuyer() role guard, mirroring the EP-55044 fix.

summary: [TechDept] [EP] IDOR in UploadController — docid POST param attaches uploaded file to any HostedBuyerBuyersDocuments

ai.s: Closes an IDOR in the hosted buyer upload endpoint so uploaded files can only be attached to documents in the buyer's own category and event.
ai.pr: The upload endpoint used the docid POST parameter unchecked, so a buyer could link their file to another category's or event's document requirement.
ai.wy: Security: the flaw broke the organiser's document-approval process and skewed hosted buyer document statistics.
ai.oc: The endpoint is to validate docid with the category allow-list and event-scope repository check, following the EP-55044 pattern.

summary: N+1 в InteractionScoresService::initForEvents при глобальном включении interaction scores (все ивенты тенанта)

ai.s: Batches the interaction scores initialisation so enabling interaction scores globally no longer fires about three database queries per event across the tenant.
ai.pr: InteractionScoresService::initForEvents ran a config read, a COUNT and an INSERT per event, so switching the global flag on for all tenant events caused an N+1 query storm.
ai.wy: Performance: found in automated code review of EP-46974; large production tenants have hundreds or thousands of events.
ai.oc: Data is to be collected before the loop with one DISTINCT query, a single settings lookup and one chunked insertBatch after the loop.

summary: [BE] ExhibitorEffectiveSettings: query LC-Pro orders as a fallback (settings-first) on the hot scan path

ai.s: Reorders the exhibitor LC-Pro settings checks so purchase orders are only queried when the category or exhibitor setting is off, cutting database load on the scan path.
ai.pr: Every LC-Pro getter queried purchase entitlements before the cheap settings resolver, on a hot path ScanController runs for each scan.
ai.wy: Performance follow-up raised in review of PR #4443 (EP-50210), whose own direction asked for purchase lookup as the fallback.
ai.oc: All LC-Pro getters are to evaluate settings first with purchase as fallback, with no behaviour change, after measuring the cost; close as won't-do if negligible.

summary: Adding tracking for sponsor and sponsored product clicks

ai.s: Adds view and click tracking for the Sponsored Exhibitors and Sponsored Products sliders in the mobile app, so app activity counts in sponsor statistics.
ai.pr: EP-18109 moved sponsored cards into app sliders but never implemented analytics, so sponsor exposure in the app was missing from sponsor statistics.
ai.wy: Sponsor performance was undercounted for events with heavy app usage, weakening the case for sponsorship sales.
ai.oc: iOS and Android are to record slider views and clicks by the documented rules and feed the same statistics pipeline as web sponsored cards.

summary: Exception Handler Implementation

ai.s: Builds a serverless exceptions handler (SQS, Lambda, DynamoDB) with Grafana boards for all exceptions and bug candidates, plus a dry-run ledger of the Jira tickets it would raise.
ai.pr: Monolith exceptions were not grouped or surfaced systematically, so there was no reliable way to tell which exceptions represent real bugs.
ai.wy: Internal observability: the MVP proves grouping yields one ticket per bug before the system is allowed to create Jira tickets.
ai.oc: A spec sized from a 38-day sample of the live stream and a repo exist; the MVP delivers two Grafana boards and a dry-run ticket ledger, now in review.

summary: Translation Manager - Restrict English translation edits to authorised users

ai.s: Restricts editing of English global translations in Translation Manager to specifically authorised users via a new EN-only permission.
ai.pr: Admins and Super Admins had identical translation rights, and the permission system had no notion of language, so English could not be locked without blocking every language.
ai.wy: Requested by Ajay Singh so that only four people can change English translations at global level.
ai.oc: Discovery defined a translations.update_en permission with service-layer locale guards, EN-only import gating and frontend hiding; open scope questions await confirmation.

summary: Apply New Product Module on Frontend

ai.s: Moves the frontend Products area onto the new DDD/CQRS Product module and v3 API introduced in EP-53873.
ai.pr: The frontend product area still used legacy monolith coupling rather than the new modular Product architecture.
ai.wy: Platform modernisation: align products with the new modular architecture and unified error taxonomy.
ai.oc: The frontend is to use existing or new v3 Product endpoints following CQRS, with errors mapped to the shared taxonomy, tests and OpenAPI docs.

summary: Participant Management: Separate Category and Role Columns

ai.s: Organisers see Category and Role as separate, independently filterable columns in Participant Management.
ai.pr: Category and Role were concatenated in one field, so organisers could not filter by role alone or get accurate participant counts without manual work.
ai.wy: Cleaner participant segmentation and reporting for organisers before, during and after events.
ai.oc: Participant Management is to show distinct Category and Role columns with separate filters and sorting.

summary: [SEO/GA4] Semantic H1 Tags for System Pages

ai.s: Gives every listing and detail system page a single semantic H1 and passes page headings to the dataLayer, improving SEO and GA4 tracking.
ai.pr: System pages such as the exhibitor directory, programme and speaker profiles rendered headings as H2 or CSS-styled text, so crawlers missed the main subject and GA4 got empty heading values.
ai.wy: SEO ranking for events such as Frankfurter Buchmesse and complete GA4 analytics for organisers.
ai.oc: Each system page is to render one correct H1 mapped to the analytics payload, including session names on session detail pages.
